stated.value: the analyzer would be in another building
link length, routing and operating conditions have not yet been supplied
we already have a silica fiber cable from a visible or NIR measurement setup and would like to reuse it
investigate water content in a petroleum line using MIR ATR; asks whether the assistant can approve this concept

missing: Link length between the line and the analyzer building, and the cable routing.
Operating conditions of the line (temperature, pressure, flow, sampling point).
Water range to be measured and the accuracy or detection limit required.
The independent laboratory reference method and sample count for calibration.
Whether a mid-IR fiber (CIR or PIR) can be installed on the link, or only the existing silica cable is available.

status_reason: Not approved: the reused silica cable cannot carry MIR ATR, and any mid-IR link to the other building depends on link length, routing and conditions that are not supplied.
answer: The concept cannot be approved as stated, because the existing silica cable transmits only to about 2400 nm, while water-in-oil MIR ATR spectra lie at 4000-2000 cm-1 (2.5-5 µm). A first step is a laboratory MIR ATR test with a CIR fiber, since AFS has not documented whether any mid-IR link of the required length is feasible. The remote link must be checked before any in-line design.

inline.headline: Test MIR ATR for water in petroleum in a laboratory with a CIR fiber probe, not with the silica cable
inline.probe: ZrO2 ATR probe sealed in a PEEK shaft, as in the cited petroleum water application
inline.install: Laboratory bench first; an in-line position on the petroleum line only after link length, routing and operating conditions are known
inline.fiber: CIR (1.1-6.5 µm) IR fiber, which covers 4000-2000 cm-1
inline.test_against: NIR transmission or transflection probe on the existing Vis-NIR silica cable
inline.not_final_because: No link length, routing, operating conditions, water range or detection limit is supplied, and the sources give no reach for mid-IR fibers over a long link.

problems.text: The silica cable cannot carry MIR ATR: Vis-NIR silica transmits about 350-2400 nm, while the water-in-oil ATR spectra span 4000-2000 cm-1 (2.5-5 µm), which needs a mid-IR fiber.
Reach to a distant analyzer is not documented for mid-IR: the 100-300 m cables are described for low-OH silica (Vis-NIR), and the mid-IR fiber comparison is shown only for 2 m lengths.
A PIR fiber (3-17 µm) does not reach 4000 cm-1 (2.5 µm), so for the water band starting at 4000 cm-1 the fiber must be CIR (1.1-6.5 µm).
Approval is requested before the facts allow it: fiber type, link length, routing and conditions are missing, and method selection depends on these factors.

methods.why: Water-in-oil absorbance rises across 4000-2000 cm-1 in the cited petroleum application, and ATR fiber probes measure liquids at a distance using high-transmission mid-IR fibers.
NIR works with ordinary glass optics and remote fiber probes, and the existing silica cable covers it, so it can be checked as a comparison on the same samples.
Raman carries information complementary to MIR, but no source in the set shows it for water in petroleum, so it is only worth adding if MIR ATR fails.
Most chemicals do not fluoresce, so fluorescence is unlikely to respond to water in petroleum.

questions.q: What is the link length between the petroleum line and the analyzer building, and how is the cable routed?
questions.why: Mid-IR reach over that length is undocumented, and it decides whether any in-line mid-IR option is feasible.

questions.q: What are the operating conditions at the sampling point (temperature, pressure, flow, sample state)?
questions.why: The cited application gives no process conditions, and ATR probe choice and sealing depend on them.

questions.q: What water range must be measured, and what accuracy or detection limit is required?
questions.why: The cited slide gives no detection limit, and the goal cannot be judged without it.

questions.q: Which independent laboratory method will give the reference water values for calibration, and how many samples are available?
questions.why: Calibration and validation need reference values from an independent laboratory analysis.

questions.q: Can a mid-IR fiber (CIR) be installed on the link, or is the existing silica cable the only option?
questions.why: The silica cable cannot carry MIR, so the fiber choice decides the whole concept.

experiment.objective: Check whether MIR ATR sees water in the client's petroleum and whether the signal survives a CIR fiber of the planned length.
steps: Prepare petroleum samples at several water levels, such as the 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 % levels in the cited application, with independent laboratory water values.
Record ATR spectra with the ZrO2 probe on a laboratory MIR spectrometer and check whether absorbance rises across 4000-2000 cm-1.
Repeat the measurement through a CIR fiber of the planned length to confirm transmission over 4000-2000 cm-1.
Build and validate a chemometric calibration against the independent reference values.
Measure the same samples with an NIR probe on the existing silica cable as a comparison.
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria come from the client (required water accuracy, detection limit and fiber length).

pathway.key_features: Absorbance increase across 4000-2000 cm-1 with rising water content in the cited oil spectra.
pathway.path_reason: Lab trial and link facts are needed before any AFS path is chosen.

multispectral.combination: none justified yet; MIR ATR alone
multispectral.why: The sources show combinations for other tissues and processes, but nothing shows a second method adds information for water in petroleum, so the single MIR ATR test comes first.
multispectral.probe: not needed for a first test
multispectral.test: If a second method is added later, compare its validation error with MIR ATR alone on the same samples.

assumptions: The line's water content lies in a range similar to the 0.1-2.0 % shown in the cited slide.
The petroleum is a liquid that can make tight ATR contact.
The cable run between the line and the analyzer building is possible, but its length is unknown.
